detector.name: Governance
detector.vulnerability_knowledge: Governance systems are vulnerable when voting power can be manipulated through flash loans or instant token acquisition, when proposal lifecycle checks use incorrect comparison operators (e.g., `<` instead of `<=` for defeat conditions), when vote reclamation lacks same-transaction reentrancy guards, when member management allows re-adding previously removed addresses without governance approval, when activation thresholds lack spam/rate limiting enabling denial-of-service via dummy proposals, when executable actions omit `msg.value` forwarding despite payable validation, when critical initialization parameters skip zero-address checks, when minting functions lack supply caps allowing arbitrary inflation of voting power, when multisig voting modifiers reset state before external calls enabling reentrancy double-voting, and when parameter setters omit bounds validation (e.g., percentage > 100). These flaws allow attackers to pass malicious proposals, block legitimate ones, drain funds, or permanently corrupt governance state.
checks: Verify voting power snapshots are taken before proposal creation and cannot be manipulated via flash loans or post-snapshot token transfers.
Ensure proposal defeat/success conditions use correct comparison operators (e.g., `forVotes <= againstVotes` for defeat, not strict `<`).
Confirm vote reclamation functions block reclaiming votes cast in the same transaction before proposal activation (check `activeProposal.proposalId` timing).
Validate member addition functions check against a removal registry or require governance approval to prevent re-adding voted-out members.
Check proposal activation requires minimum endorsement thresholds AND rate limiting (e.g., cooldown, reputation) to prevent spam activation.
Verify executable action functions forward `msg.value` via `{value: actionInfo.value}` when the action is payable and validates `msg.value == actionInfo.value`.
Ensure initialization functions validate all critical address parameters (vetoer, treasury, token) against `address(0)`.
Confirm minting/issuance functions for governance tokens enforce a hard cap on `totalSupply` or require governance approval for inflation.

incorrect_example.explanation: Missing spam protection: any proposal meeting ENDORSEMENT_THRESHOLD becomes sole active proposal, allowing dummy proposals to block legitimate ones via GRACE_PERIOD lockout.

correct_example.explanation: Added ACTIVATION_COOLDOWN and MIN_SUBMITTER_REPUTATION checks to prevent spam activation and denial-of-service via dummy proposals.
